\section*{N0005: initial representatives and the literal initial-data class}
\textbf{Status: DRAFT; Lean NOT\_RUN.} The source audited here is the complete serialized text of Wang, arXiv:2212.13343v1, dated 27 December 2022, PDF pages 1--34. No external version comparison, shell execution, or Lean execution is claimed.

\paragraph{Precise trace lemma.}
Let $1<p<\infty$, $p'=p/(p-1)$, and let $u(t)$ take values in $L^p(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb R^m)$ for almost every $t\in(0,T)$, with
\[
M:=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{0<t<T}\|u(t)\|_{L^p}<\infty.
\]
Assume $\rho_0\in L^\infty_{\rm loc}$ and that, along a common full-measure set $E$ of admissible times,
\[
\|\rho(t)-\rho_0\|_{L^\infty(K)}\longrightarrow0
\quad(t\downarrow0,\ t\in E)
\]
for every compact $K$. Suppose $m_0:=\rho_0u_0\in L^1_{\rm loc}$ and
\[
\int\rho(t)u(t)\cdot\varphi\,dx\longrightarrow
\int m_0\cdot\varphi\,dx
\qquad(\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb R^m)).
\]
Then there exists $v\in L^p$ satisfying
\[
\rho_0v=m_0\quad\text{a.e.},\qquad \|v\|_{L^p}\le M.
\]
In particular, if $\rho_0>0$ almost everywhere, then $u_0=v$ almost everywhere and $\|u_0\|_{L^p}\le M$.

Here local uniform convergence is understood in the usual locally bounded density setting. If that phrase is intended to allow unbounded functions with bounded differences, local boundedness of $\rho_0$ must be stated separately; the proof uses it explicitly. Wang's density regularity supplies this property.

\paragraph{Proof.}
Enlarge the exceptional null set so that $\|u(t)\|_p\le M$ on $E$. Choose recursively $t_n\in E$ with
\[
0<t_n<\min\{T,1/n,t_{n-1}/2\}.
\]
Every such interval intersects $E$, because $E$ has full measure. Reflexivity of the vector-valued $L^p$ space gives a subsequence, still denoted $t_n$, and $v\in L^p$ such that $u(t_n)\rightharpoonup v$. Weak lower semicontinuity yields $\|v\|_p\le M$.

Fix $\varphi\in C_c^\infty$ and put $K=\operatorname{supp}\varphi$. Since $\rho_0\varphi\in L^{p'}$, weak convergence gives
\[
\int u(t_n)\cdot\rho_0\varphi\,dx\longrightarrow
\int v\cdot\rho_0\varphi\,dx.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\left|\int u(t_n)\cdot(\rho(t_n)-\rho_0)\varphi\,dx\right|
\le M\|\rho(t_n)-\rho_0\|_{L^\infty(K)}\|\varphi\|_{p'}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The assumed conservative trace therefore identifies $\rho_0v$ and $m_0$ as distributions. Both are locally integrable, so they agree almost everywhere. On $\{\rho_0>0\}$ division gives $v=u_0$. This proves the assertion. No unweighted strong initial convergence is used.

If vacuum has positive measure, the conclusion only fixes $v$ on $\{\rho_0>0\}$; it does not imply that the specified values of $u_0$ on vacuum belong to $L^p$. One may set $v=0$ on vacuum without increasing its norm.

\paragraph{Mapping to Wang's stated solution class.}
On PDF page 3, (1.8) asserts $u\in L^\infty(0,T^*;L^{q_2})$, with $\alpha=\min\{a/2,1\}$ and $q_2=4/\alpha$ in (1.9). Since $a>1$, one has $1/2<\alpha\le1$ and $4\le q_2<8$, so the trace lemma applies with a finite reflexive exponent.

The same display asserts $\rho\in C([0,T^*];W^{1,q}(\mathbb R^2))$, $q>2$. The continuous Sobolev embedding $W^{1,q}(\mathbb R^2)\hookrightarrow L^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$ implies
\[
\|\rho(t)-\rho(0)\|_\infty\le C_q\|\rho(t)-\rho(0)\|_{W^{1,q}}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Identifying $\rho(0)=\rho_0$ uses the density initial condition in (1.3), PDF page 2. The momentum part of (1.3) supplies the conservative trace under its ordinary distributional initial-value interpretation. Definition 1.1 alone, which concerns equations on the open time interval, does not itself specify a trace. Thus the application is explicitly conditional on interpreting “solution of (1.1), (1.3), (1.4)” as attaining the displayed conservative initial data.

Consequently, any solution attaining (1.3) and satisfying (1.8) necessarily admits an $L^{q_2}$ representative of its initial velocity on positive density. If $\rho_0>0$ almost everywhere, necessarily $u_0\in L^{q_2}$.

\paragraph{Verification of the proposed data.}
Fix $A>0$, $c\in\mathbb R^2\setminus\{0\}$, and set
\[
\rho_0(x)=Ae^{-|x|^2},\qquad u_0(x)=c,\qquad\theta_0(x)=0.
\]
These data meet every explicitly displayed hypothesis of Theorem 1.1 on PDF page 3:

For every $a>1$ and $\eta_0>0$, $f=\bar x^a\rho_0$ is nonnegative and smooth. Writing $s=e+|x|^2$, its logarithmic derivative is
\[
\nabla\log f=-2x+\frac{ax}{s}
+\frac{2a(1+\eta_0)x}{s\log s}.
\]
Thus $f$ and its first derivatives have at most polynomial and logarithmic growth multiplied by a Gaussian; they belong to every finite $L^r$, including $L^1$, $L^2$, and $L^q$. Hence $\bar x^a\rho_0\in L^1\cap H^1\cap W^{1,q}$ for every finite $q>2$.

Furthermore,
\[
\|\sqrt{\rho_0}u_0\|_2^2=A\pi|c|^2<\infty,
\qquad \sqrt{\rho_0}\theta_0=0,
\qquad \nabla u_0=0\in H^1,
\qquad \nabla\theta_0=0\in L^2.
\]
The temperature is nonnegative. Every term on the left of compatibility condition (1.7) vanishes, so $g=0\in L^2$ satisfies it exactly. The density is positive everywhere but has no positive uniform lower bound. If unit mass is desired for the normalization used on page 16, take $A=1/\pi$.

The initial physical energy is
\[
E_0=\int\left(\tfrac12\rho_0|u_0|^2+c_\nu\rho_0\theta_0\right)dx
=\tfrac12A\pi|c|^2.
\]
It can be arbitrarily small with $c\ne0$, including at unit mass. This observation is only a data check; it does not establish a global theorem or a new blowup theorem.

For every finite $p$, $u_0\notin L^p(\mathbb R^2)$, since $|c|^p$ has infinite integral. Because $\rho_0>0$ everywhere, the trace lemma rules out a solution with these conservative initial data and the asserted uniform $L^{q_2}$ velocity bound. This obstruction already concerns the stated local class.

\paragraph{Audit of restrictions throughout the serialized source.}
The initial condition (1.3), page 2, prescribes density, momentum, and thermal density. The far-field condition (1.4) on that page explicitly has $t>0$ and says “in some weak sense.” It does not explicitly impose $u_0\to0$ as $|x|\to\infty$. Theorem 1.1 supplies no separate $u_0\in L^p$, closure-of-compact-support, or normalized-representative hypothesis. Definition 1.1 supplies no such hypothesis either.

Pages 5--16 impose zero boundary values and compactly supported approximations for bounded-domain auxiliary problems; these are conditions on approximants, not an explicit additional hypothesis on the original $u_0$. The displayed convergence (3.61), page 16, measures $\nabla u_0$ and $\sqrt{\rho_0}u_0$, which retain the constant-velocity data. Pages 17--22 add $\theta_0\in L^2$ for the damping problem, a condition already satisfied by $\theta_0=0$. The initial approximations (4.27)--(4.29), pages 22--23, again concern derivative and density-weighted norms. Pages 24--32 study continuation of the solution already asserted by Theorem 1.1; they do not introduce an initial representative restriction repairing its original statement. Pages 32--34 contain references, whose cited contents are not supplied and are not independently verified here.

Accordingly, within the complete serialized v1 text, no explicit original-data restriction excluding this example was found. A tacit requirement that (1.4) also hold at $t=0$ would exclude it, but would add a restriction beyond the displayed time range. A homogeneous completion or a chosen decaying representative might also exclude it; the source does not explicitly identify that as the original-data class.

\paragraph{Location of a representative issue in the proof.}
Lemma 2.4, page 6, states its weighted inequality only for $C_c^\infty$ functions. On page 20, Lemma 4.1 applies it to $u$ to infer $\|u\|_{L^{q_2}}$ from weighted gradient bounds. Such an extension needs control of the additive representative. The constant function has zero weighted gradient and is not in any finite unweighted $L^p$; hence the compact-support inequality cannot extend to all locally Sobolev representatives solely from weighted-gradient finiteness. This identifies an obligation at that step, without proving that every preceding construction is invalid. The trace obstruction independently shows that a successful extension and the stated initial trace cannot coexist for the proposed data.

\paragraph{Scope of the conclusion.}
Under the ordinary conservative initial-trace interpretation, the literal displayed hypotheses of Wang v1 include data incompatible with its asserted solution class. This is a statement-level mismatch established by the draft trace argument and the explicit data check. It does not prove nonexistence in a different homogeneous or normalized solution class, does not audit later versions, and does not settle the full small-energy global problem. No child node is unlocked by this unformalized audit.
findings_zh: N0005 的代表元结论有完整弱紧性证明，并得到范数界 ||v||ₚ≤ess sup ||u(t)||ₚ；不需要无权速度强初始收敛。密度局部有界及保守初始迹的具体含义已明确。
Wang v1 的 (1.8) 与 (1.3) 按通常保守初始迹解释，强制正密度区域上的初始速度具有 L^{q₂} 代表元；密度处处正时强制 u₀∈L^{q₂}。
高斯密度、非零常速度、零温度满足 (1.6)、(1.7) 的全部显式条件，兼容函数可取 g=0；物理初始能量可任意小，但常速度不属于任何有限指数无权 Lᵖ。
已检查所给完整 34 页序列化文本；未发现明确排除上述初值的原始代表元条件。(1.4) 明写 t>0，把远场条件延伸到 t=0 属于额外解释。
上述矛盾针对原文显式初值条件与所宣称局部解类的组合。研究证明为 DRAFT，Lean 为 NOT_RUN；不能据此开放子节点或宣称其他解类不存在。

formalizable_lemmas: N0005 candidate: for 1<p<∞, a uniformly Lᵖ-bounded sequence uₙ, locally L∞ densities ρₙ converging locally in L∞ to ρ₀, and ρₙuₙ converging distributionally to m₀∈L¹_loc, there exists v∈Lᵖ with ρ₀v=m₀ almost everywhere and ||v||ₚ bounded by the sequence bound.
Positive-density specialization: if ρ₀>0 almost everywhere and m₀=ρ₀u₀, the preceding representative equals u₀ almost everywhere.
Admissible-time extraction: every full-measure subset of (0,T) contains a strictly decreasing sequence tending to zero.
Product identification: local L∞ convergence of scalar multipliers and weak Lᵖ convergence of vector fields imply distributional convergence of their products.

Explicit data verification: weighted Gaussian density satisfies the stated finite-exponent first-order Sobolev requirements, while a nonzero constant velocity has finite Gaussian-weighted kinetic energy and fails every finite unweighted Lᵖ requirement.
